key_insight: Post-optimization corrections can substantially improve ADAPT-VQE results without adding new ansatz layers or running another nonlinear optimization.
engineering_relevance: These methods reduce both circuit depth and measurement cost, making chemically relevant quantum simulations more practical on near-term hardware.
method: Hamiltonian-moment Krylov subspace diagonalization is applied after ADAPT-VQE optimization to refine energies.
Identity-augmented q-sc-EOM corrects truncated or sampled ADAPT-VQE states to recover accuracy.
Both approaches act as post-processing steps, so they avoid further ansatz growth.
evidence_signal: Across molecular systems up to 20 qubits, first-order Krylov correction reduced the iterations needed to reach the 1.6 mE_h threshold by up to about 6× and reduced measurement cost by up to about 40×.
watch_item: Performance depends on state quality and cost-model assumptions, so gains may be smaller when gradients are noisy or the underlying ansatz is extremely limited.
paper_title: Post-Optimization Subspace Corrections to Quantum Ansätze
